cities.base: Stay central near Durbar Square/Thamel for walkable access to the old city sights.
cities.name: Kathmandu

cities.base: Lakeside, for evening views of Phewa Lake and easy access to Sarangkot and Kande taxis.
cities.name: Pokhara

cities.base: Day trip from Kathmandu, best preserved of the three squares.
cities.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square

cities.base: Sunrise viewpoint reached by taxi from Pokhara lakeside.
cities.name: Sarangkot

cities.base: Trailhead for the Australian Camp/Dhampus day hike, reached by taxi from Pokhara.
cities.name: Kande / Australian Camp

places.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
places.note: The best preserved of the three squares, worth the day more than a second pass through Kathmandu's.

places.name: Kande short loop (wind/weather backup)
places.note: A 1.5 hr out-and-back on the lower switchbacks below Australian Camp for days when cloud or wind rules out the full ascent. Forest walking, no view payoff, just movement and air.

places.name: Australian Camp to Dhampus extension
places.note: Extends the day hike another 1.5-2 hrs through a working Gurung village with terraced fields, adds distance and mild elevation but no technical difficulty. Good add-on if energy allows before the drive back.

places.name: Kande to Australian Camp
places.note: Round trip about 3-3.5 hrs including return, roughly 400m elevation gain from Kande. Clear-day views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre from the camp clearing, worst on cloudy afternoons when the range disappears entirely.

places.name: Kande Trailhead
places.note: Start point for the Australian Camp/Dhampus route, about an hour drive from Pokhara lakeside. Steep stone steps for the first 40 minutes, no permit checkpoint on this short route.

places.name: Sarangkot Cable Car
places.note: A cable car up to Sarangkot has been proposed and discussed for years but as of now does not operate. Skip planning around it, the drive or walk up is still how everyone gets there.

places.name: Annapurna Range Full Panorama Deck
places.note: The main upper tower deck itself, the widest sweep of the range from Dhaulagiri to Annapurna II on a clear morning. This is the postcard shot everyone is there for, get there early or you're photographing the backs of other people's phones.

places.name: Sarangkot Taxi Stand (Pokhara pickup point)
places.note: Where drivers from Pokhara lakeside drop off and wait during the sunrise run. Not a sight, just useful to know the layout since most taxis wait here rather than at the summit itself, adding a short walk up.

places.name: Zip Flyer Pokhara (Sarangkot to Hemja)
places.note: Claims to be one of the world's steepest zip lines, launching from the Sarangkot ridge. Skip for this itinerary, it eats a chunk of the day and money for a thrill ride that has nothing to do with why you're up here, which is the mountain view.

places.name: Sarangkot Sunset Viewing
places.note: Same viewpoint, evening version, facing Pokhara valley and the lake below rather than the peaks. Fewer crowds than sunrise since most tour groups only come once, but the mountains themselves don't light up the way they do at dawn, this is the fallback if a sunrise trip gets clouded out or the group can't manage the early start.

places.name: Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South Panorama Point
places.note: A few meters west of the main tower, slightly less crowded angle on Machhapuchhre's fishtail peak and the Annapurna South massif. Same view as the main platform, worth trying if the tower deck is packed.

places.name: Sarangkot Lodge Row
places.note: Cluster of small guesthouses along the ridge road, mostly used by trekkers overnighting to catch sunrise without the pre-dawn taxi from Pokhara. Worth knowing about if a driver cancels or the group wants to skip the early departure, not worth a special visit otherwise.

places.name: View Top Sunrise Restaurant
places.note: Simple teahouse right by the viewpoint serving milk tea, instant coffee and basic Nepali breakfast (eggs, toast, momos). Nothing special about the food itself, the point is sitting down with the view while the crowd thins.

places.name: Sarangkot Paragliding Launch Site
places.note: Tandem paragliding flights launch from this ridge above Sarangkot village, landing near Phewa Lake in Pokhara. Weather dependent and usually booked through a Pokhara agency rather than walked up to, mornings after the sunrise crowd clears tend to have calmer wind for launch.

places.name: Sarangkot Village Trail
places.note: Stone stairway path connecting the lower village to the viewpoint, lined with small terraced farms and a handful of teahouses. Good way to walk off the sunrise crowd rather than taxi straight back down.

places.name: Sarangkot Fort (Kot)
places.note: Ruined hilltop fort just above the main viewpoint, remnant of a old Kaski kingdom stronghold. Little signage and not much structure left standing, but almost nobody walks the extra five minutes up to it so it's a quieter spot for the same view.

places.name: Sarangkot Sunrise Viewpoint
places.note: Concrete tower and terraced platforms facing the Annapurna range and Machhapuchhre. Crowded with tour buses in peak season, arrive 30-40 min before sunrise to get a spot on the upper deck. Clouds kill the view a fair share of mornings, worth checking the forecast the night before.

places.name: Changu Narayan Temple
places.note: Oldest temple in the valley and genuinely worth seeing, but it needs its own half day with the drive and there isn't slack for it on a one-day Bhaktapur trip built around the main squares.

places.name: Cafe Nyatapola
places.note: Rooftop seating in a converted pagoda-style building right on Taumadhi Square, food is average but the view over the square at lunch is the reason to sit here.

places.name: Juju Dhau tasting near Durbar Square
places.note: King curd, a thick set yogurt in a clay bowl, Bhaktapur's signature food. Sold everywhere around the square, no need to seek a specific shop.

places.name: Pujari Math / National Art Gallery of Wood Carving
places.note: Small museum of wood carvings inside a former monastery building, right next to the Peacock Window, worth the short stop if the door is open.

places.name: Peacock Window
places.note: Single carved wooden window on a side street near Dattatreya Square, called the finest woodcarving in the valley. Small, easy to walk past.

places.name: Dattatreya Square
places.note: Quieter third square, a walk east from the main one, fewer vendors and fewer tourists.

places.name: Pottery Square
places.note: Rows of clay pots drying in the sun, potters still working wheels by hand. Buy direct if you want something small and unbreakable to carry.

places.name: Bhairabnath Temple
places.note: Squat, heavily rebuilt temple facing Nyatapola across the square, interior not open to non-Hindus.

places.name: Nyatapola Temple
places.note: Five-tier pagoda, tallest in Nepal, survived the 2015 earthquake essentially intact. Steps up the plinth are fine to sit on.

places.name: Golden Gate (Sun Dhoka)
places.note: Small gilded gateway into the palace courtyard, easy to miss if you don't look up, worth the thirty seconds.

places.name: 55 Window Palace (Palace of Fifty-Five Windows)
places.note: Facade alone is the draw, carved wood windows from the Malla era, part of the same ticketed complex.

places.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
places.note: Entry fee covers the whole city zone for the day, not just the square. Come early before tour groups arrive from Kathmandu.

places.name: Bindhyabasini Temple
places.note: Working Hindu temple on a small hill in the old bazaar, actual local worship rather than a tourist stop. Worth a stop only if you're already in the old town, out of the way from Lakeside.

places.name: Lakeside Promenade Sunset Walk
places.note: Simple stroll along the eastern shore of Phewa Lake as the light drops. Free, unhurried, a good way to close the free day without needing a plan.

places.name: Boomerang Restaurant and German Bakery
places.note: Long-running Lakeside spot with a garden setting, mixed Nepali and Western menu. Reliable dinner after a long hiking day, nothing fancy.

places.name: Lakeside (Pokhara's Thamel)
places.note: The strip along the lake, trekking gear shops, bars, restaurants. Fine for an evening walk and a beer, not a destination in its own right for anyone who dislikes souvenir shopping.

places.name: Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave
places.note: Limestone cave with a Shiva shrine, connects underground toward Davis Falls. Damp and slippery in sections, worth it paired with the falls if you're already there, not worth a special trip alone.

places.name: Davis Falls (Patale Chhango)
places.note: Small waterfall, most dramatic right after monsoon and underwhelming otherwise. Skip unless combining with the adjacent cave since it takes ten minutes and adds little.

places.name: Paragliding from Sarangkot
places.note: Tandem flights launch from Sarangkot and land near Phewa Lake. Weather dependent, mornings are usually more stable than afternoons. Optional add for the free day, not for anyone uneasy with heights.

places.name: International Mountain Museum
places.note: Good rainy-day option, covers Nepal's mountaineering history and Sherpa culture in real depth. A bit out of the way, worth a taxi if the weather kills outdoor plans.

places.name: Kande Trailhead (Australian Camp / Dhampus route)
places.note: About an hour drive from Lakeside. Steep stone-step climb to Australian Camp (roughly 2-3 hrs up), then loop back via Dhampus. No permit required for this short version. Good food stops at Australian Camp teahouses.

places.name: Sarangkot Sunrise Viewpoint
places.note: Taxi up in the dark, arrive before first light. Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range if the sky cooperates, which it does not always do, check cloud forecast the night before.

places.name: World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa)
places.note: Reachable by boat across the lake then a 30-40 min uphill walk, or a longer taxi round the far side. View over the lake and Annapurna range on a clear day, crowds are thin compared to Sarangkot.

places.name: Phewa Lake Boating Dock (Baidam)
places.note: Rent a plain rowboat by the hour, no guide needed. Water is calmer and prettier in morning light but afternoon works fine before sunset.

places.name: Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple)
places.note: Go before 10am, the monkeys and the heat both get worse as the day goes on.

places.name: Patan Museum
places.note: Bronze and religious art collection inside a restored courtyard building within Patan Durbar Square, one of the better-curated museums in the country and a solid indoor option if weather turns on day 7.

places.name: Stupa View Restaurant
places.note: Rooftop tea or beer directly facing Boudhanath stupa, good spot to sit as the evening butter-lamp circuit picks up around the base. Not fine dining, you're paying for the view.

places.name: Narayanhiti Palace Museum
places.note: Former royal palace, now a museum showing the rooms roughly as they were including the 2001 massacre site. Interesting if you're into the monarchy's end, skippable if time is tight, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

places.name: Kasthamandap
places.note: The original pavilion the city is named for collapsed in the 2015 earthquake and what stands now is a rebuild. Worth a glance while already in Durbar Square, not a special trip.

places.name: Chandragiri Hills cable car
places.note: Cable car up to a ridge with, on a clear day, a wide Himalayan panorama including Everest far in the distance. Honest note: haze cuts visibility most of the year, so this is a weather gamble, not a guaranteed view like Sarangkot.

places.name: Momo tasting at Yangling Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Small no-frills Tibetan spot for momos and thukpa, a real lunch break between Durbar Square and Swayambhunath rather than a tourist buffet.

places.name: Freak Street
places.note: Old hippie-trail street just south of Kathmandu Durbar Square, quieter and less commercial than Thamel now. Nothing to buy that matters, just a short walk to see where the 1970s overland trail ended up.

places.name: Bhojan Griha
places.note: Restored Rana-era house serving a set Newari feast with a folk dance show. Touristy but the food is legitimately good and the building itself is worth the visit, book ahead.

places.name: Thamel
places.note: Trekking gear shops, bars, and souvenir stalls packed into narrow lanes. Fine for an hour after dinner or to buy a last-minute duffel bag, skip if souvenir shopping isn't your thing as the sales pressure is constant.

places.name: Pashupatinath Temple
places.note: Non-Hindus can't enter the main temple but the riverside ghats are visible from across the Bagmati, including cremations in progress. Sobering rather than pretty, and the touts offering to be your 'guide' at the entrance are relentless.

places.name: Boudhanath Stupa
places.note: One of the largest stupas in the world, ringed by rooftop cafes for tea and a slow circumambulation. Late afternoon light on the whitewash is better than midday glare. Pair with a butter tea stop at one of the rooftop restaurants overlooking the stupa.

places.name: Patan Durbar Square
places.note: Quieter and better museum than the Kathmandu square, good low-key last day before an early flight.

places.name: Australian Camp / Dhampus
places.note: No permit needed for this short version, clear-day views of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South.

places.name: Sarangkot Sunrise Viewpoint
places.note: The payoff view of the whole trip, but cloud cover kills it often, check the forecast the night before.

places.name: World Peace Pagoda
places.note: Free, and a decent afternoon pairing with the lake.

places.name: Phewa Lake
places.note: Pleasant, not dramatic, good for slowing down.

places.name: Kathmandu Durbar Square
places.note: Still visibly under earthquake repair in places, don't expect it pristine.

places.name: Kande to Pokhara taxi return
places.note: Drive back down to Pokhara lakeside, about an hour depending on traffic through Phedi. Arrange the return pickup time with the driver before starting the hike, phone signal at Australian Camp is unreliable.

places.name: Mardi Himal trailhead extension
places.note: Skip: this is the start of a genuine multi-day trek, not a feasible add-on to the single day hike out of Kande. Don't let a guide talk you into 'just a bit further'.

places.name: Annapurna Conservation Area entry (skip for this route)
places.note: Skip: the short Australian Camp/Dhampus loop from Kande does not require the ACAP permit or TIMS card that longer Annapurna treks need, don't waste time or money arranging one for this day.

places.name: Dhampus village walk
places.note: Stone paths through a real Gurung and Magar settlement still lived in year-round, not staged for visitors, prayer flags and terraced barley fields. Worth a slow pass through rather than a rush.

places.name: Kande roadside shop stop
places.note: Small shop at the trailhead for water and snacks before starting, last easy resupply point until Australian Camp itself.

places.name: Pothana ridge viewpoint
places.note: A quieter alternative view a bit further along the ridge from Australian Camp, fewer people, similar range visible on a clear morning. Adds real walking time, only worth it if not tight on schedule.

places.name: Australian Camp viewpoint clearing
places.note: The actual payoff spot, an open field facing the Annapurna range. Go before 11am, afternoon haze in the valley usually rolls in and flattens the view.

places.name: Australian Camp teahouse lunch stop
places.note: Basic dal bhat and milk tea at one of the lodges at the top. Menu and price are near-identical across all of them, nobody comes here for the food.

outings.why: Both are half-day sights that fit in one day if you start at 8am, before the monkeys and heat build up at Swayambhunath.
outings.name: Kathmandu Durbar Square + Swayambhunath

outings.why: The best preserved of the three Durbar Squares, worth a full day including the drive rather than a second pass through Kathmandu's.
outings.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square day trip

outings.why: Pleasant, not dramatic, a good half day to slow down with a boat on the lake and the pagoda above it.
outings.name: Phewa Lake and World Peace Pagoda
outings.fallback: Skip the boat and just walk the lakeside promenade.

outings.why: The payoff mountain view of the whole trip, but cloud cover kills it often so check the forecast the night before.
outings.name: Sarangkot sunrise
outings.fallback: Sleep in and do the International Mountain Museum instead.

outings.why: Real Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South views without a trekking permit, the closest thing to actual trekking this trip fits.
outings.name: Australian Camp / Dhampus day hike
outings.fallback: Shorten to just Australian Camp and skip Dhampus if legs or weather are against you.

outings.why: Quieter and better-run museum than the Kathmandu square, an easy low-key day before an early flight home.
outings.name: Patan Durbar Square

destination.name: Nepal
destination.pitch: Eight days isn't enough for Everest Base Camp or an Annapurna trek, so this is Kathmandu's old cities plus a permit-free taste of the Annapurna foothills from Pokhara instead.
destination.caveat: Two of your eight days evaporate in transit and the KTM-Pokhara flight cancels often enough in poor visibility that you shouldn't schedule anything tight around it. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Kathmandu's old city and Thamel give you dense, chaotic urban texture if you want it, though it's not the reason to come.
because.nature: Sarangkot sunrise and the Australian Camp/Dhampus day hike give real Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South views with no trekking permit required.
because.culture: Three medieval Durbar Squares, Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, and Patan, each a genuinely different city-state's old palace core, not a repeat of the same thing.
because.relaxation: Phewa Lake is pleasant and slow if you need a half day off after the temples.
